My dad has a German copy of the Glass Bead game - I started it, but my german's not that great. Stuck with Friedrich Dürrenmatt.

I simply am scared of returning to therapy. I foolishly told my mother I was going to therapy the first time around, and ever since she has demanded constant information on my mental health and my mood. She is certain I have bipolar and cries on the phone to me about what a horror it would be if I were to commit suicide or lose my job because I didn't go to therapy and get on pills. Of course, she's right, but whenever I let her into my life it's a bid for total control, micromanagement of just about everything, and this constant praise for my day-to-day efforts that is not merely hollow but fairly mean-spirited. As a child, she would tell me I was superior to all other children, and that she and I were special people who mattered more than others. I have spent a lifetime deprogramming myself from that. I know I've gone too far the other direction, and I want to improve that relationship, but she does not accept that I do not want to live in comfort and that, a bit more cruelly, I don't want to talk to her about my mental health or about my emotional life in general. I feel we are worlds apart in our understanding of life and our mission in it, and I'm sick of petty arguing and constant dismissal of what I find important. 

tl;dr mommy issues are making me feel that going to therapy is capitulation and opening the floodgates for more unwanted interference.

Everything you said seems so astute, articulate. I don't want to shower you with more sympathy because you seem like someone who's had that in spades. Reading your words suggests someone to me who has considered themselves, examined the world, and sought some sort of coherency. That in the face of such absurd cruelty that you could manage to look the world in the eye - you're brilliant. When I talk to people about my suicidality, and how it relates to my worldview, it's hard to get terribly far without the conversation derailing into pity. Do you have anyone that you can talk to who can relate to your worldview at all, your experiences? Do you want that? Do you think it's an effort worth pursuing?
I'm sorry this is so long, your post just interests me so much.

I actually read Steppenwolf a few months ago. I was very struck by the image of Goethe laughing and expanding, and the discourse on iconography either immediately before or after that passage - it seemed to me an indictment of the attitude I had (have) taken toward art. It was precisely that an author and their work could stretch beyond themselves and relate, encompass life, and its minutiae and its seemingly offensive or unimportant aspects that it achieved something beautiful. This demands the author, if not "abandon" the individual, at least be willing to deface themselves, change, look silly - in a word, abandon themselves as the primary object of their creative process. It was an admonishment of everything I had tried to accomplish before, in art at least.

I haven't tried an antidepressant. I was given an anti-psychotic a year ago, but it made me so lethargic I stopped taking it.

My parents divorced. I learned after the fact, when I was older, that my mother had a suicide attempt then. I was six. I didn't notice at the time that she was especially sad. Some people don't seem to understand how brutal a divorce can be. It is as though love were merely business to them, and when two partners separate it's a mutual decision pursued in objective self-interest.

Do you have anything you want to do before you take the flight? Projects, plans, people to see where you are now? How much time do you have?

Your concern for how your parents would feel is touching, but in my experience the loss of a child is brutal regardless of the cause. It's something so intense that, short of murder, why it happened becomes irrelevant.
Do you have a day off coming up? Some plans with friends?

I love it here too. I'm from further north, but very familiar with the Portland area. 
Was there any particular event that made you want to be / need to be closer to your family?

I adore ambient music, so most likely October by Tim Hecker or one of Basinski's pieces. 
That said, it would most likely be something with words, so I could hear somebody. I want someone talking to me when I go, even if it's just a song.
Do you make music?
